hypothesis: Complete row-lexicographic and per-row reflection symmetry breaking will remove enough equivalent assignments from the full scope-111 one-hot CNF for Kissat to produce a validator-accepted witness within the bounded solver run.
rationale: The prior full-domain Kissat encoding only ordered the first positive mark, leaving permutations among rows with equal prefixes and reflection-equivalent normalized rows. These are exact symmetries: row permutation preserves the difference set, and reflecting a normalized row preserves every absolute within-row difference. Strengthening only these redundant constraints tests whether the previous timeout was caused by avoidable symmetry rather than by changing the mathematical decision problem.
expected_information_gain: SAT followed by independent verification would produce true-objective progress at scope<=111. UNSAT would certify only the finite frozen scope-111 instance. UNKNOWN or timeout would close this stronger encoding at the declared budget and would not establish infeasibility.
method: Generate a DIMACS CNF for seven normalized six-mark rows with positive marks one-hot in 1..111, strict within-row order, complete lexicographic ordering of all five positive-mark coordinates between adjacent rows, the per-row reflection rule a1+a4<=a5, one auxiliary literal for each possible within-row difference occurrence, and pairwise at-most-one constraints across all occurrences of each difference. Run Kissat 4.0.3 under WSL2 Ubuntu with a 120-second solver limit. Decode any SAT model using the preserved mark-variable IDs and independently validate it with the repository integer verifier.
metric: SAT status, formula size, symmetry-clause counts as reflected by the formula, elapsed time, decoded rows, and independent DTS validity
metric_relation_to_true_objective: A decoded assignment accepted by the independent integer verifier with scope<=111 is exactly true-objective progress. UNSAT establishes finite full-instance infeasibility only; UNKNOWN or timeout establishes no mathematical infeasibility.

configuration.encoding: one-hot marks plus explicit difference-occurrence auxiliaries and pairwise at-most-one
configuration.symmetry_break: complete row lexicographic order plus per-row reflection a1+a4<=a5

kill_condition: Stop at SAT, UNSAT, or the 120-second Kissat limit plus bounded process cleanup. Do not infer mathematical infeasibility from UNKNOWN or timeout.

baseline_comparison.expected_relation: strict improvement only if SAT model passes independent verifier

previous_best_comparison.full_kissat: UNKNOWN under 120-second budget with first-mark-only ordering
previous_best_comparison.full_cadical: UNKNOWN under 120-second budget with first-mark-only ordering
previous_best_comparison.expected_relation: same finite decision problem with strictly stronger exact symmetry reduction

interpretation: Kissat returned UNKNOWN at the declared 120-second limit on the symmetry-strengthened full scope-111 formula. No model was emitted, so the target was not reached and no mathematical infeasibility follows.
failure_mode: The stronger exact symmetry encoding remained unresolved at the bounded Kissat solver limit; this is a solver-budget result, not an UNSAT certificate.
what_was_learned: Complete lexicographic row ordering and per-row reflection breaking were soundly added and generated a reproducible 15570-variable, 2383982-clause formula. Kissat still returned UNKNOWN after 119.34 solver seconds, so the prior timeout cannot be attributed solely to the two tested symmetry omissions. The primary and independent verifiers both rejected the empty decode because no assignment was available.
recommended_next_action: Close this symmetry-strengthened Kissat budget as inconclusive. Do not infer finite or global DTS infeasibility; reallocate only to a materially different exact encoding or solver capability, a structural proof route, or a human-supplied construction.
repetition_justification: This is not a repeat of the prior full Kissat or CaDiCaL runs: the finite instance is unchanged, but the encoding adds complete lexicographic row ordering and per-row reflection breaking that were absent from both prior formulas.
